description: Those whose thought is on the Lord, awakening one another and always speaking of him, are content and take delight (tuṣyanti ca ramanti ca) (10.9).
The Lord declares that Arjuna cannot see him with his own eye and gives him a divine eye (divyaṃ cakṣuḥ) to behold his sovereign yoga (11.8).
notes: Merged from extractor A's phn:bhagavad-gita-divine-eye and extractor B's phn:bhagavad-gita-divine-eye-granted (both 11.8).

description: The radiance of the form is likened to that of a thousand suns rising at once in the sky (11.12); it is a mass of splendour blazing on every side with the brilliance of fire and sun, hard to look at (11.17), heating the universe (11.19), filling the world with fierce rays (11.30), 'made of splendour' (11.47).
notes: Merged from extractor A's phn:bhagavad-gita-light-of-a-thousand-suns (11.12, 11.17) and extractor B's phn:bhagavad-gita-radiance-of-a-thousand-suns (11.12–47).

description: Told to be without fear and with a glad mind, Arjuna sees again the Lord's own gentle, human form and says he is now composed (sacetāḥ) and has returned to his natural state (prakṛti) (11.49–51).
notes: Merged from extractor A's phn:bhagavad-gita-return-to-own-nature (11.49–51) and extractor B's phn:bhagavad-gita-return-to-composure (11.50–51).

description: Seeing the terrible form the worlds tremble and so does Arjuna (11.20, 11.23); shaken in his inmost being he finds neither steadiness nor calm (11.24), loses his bearings and finds no shelter, and begs the Lord to be gracious (11.25); he trembles and stammers in great fear (11.35); his manas is shaken with fear and he asks to see the former form (11.45–46). The Lord bids him not be distressed or bewildered and to be free of fear (11.49), and consoles him by resuming his gentle form (11.50).
notes: Merged from extractor A's phn:bhagavad-gita-shaken-by-the-fierce-form (kind 'state') and extractor B's phn:bhagavad-gita-terror-before-the-universal-form (kind 'difficulty'); 'difficulty' is kept because the text treats the terror as a disturbance the Lord removes (11.49–50). The verses' word is pravyathita, 'shaken' (11.20, 11.23, 11.24).

description: Filled with amazement (vismaya), his hair standing on end (hṛṣṭaromā), Arjuna bows his head with joined palms (11.14); after the Lord declares himself Time he trembles, bows, prostrates and speaks stammering, greatly afraid (11.35); he says he is thrilled (hṛṣita) at seeing what was never seen before, while his mind (manas) is shaken with fear (11.45).
notes: Merged from extractor A's phn:bhagavad-gita-signs-in-arjuna-at-the-vision (11.14, 11.35) and extractor B's phn:bhagavad-gita-wonder-and-horripilation (11.14, 11.45).

description: Arjuna sees the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra with the kings, Bhīṣma, Droṇa, Karṇa and warriors of his own side rushing into the Lord's mouths, some caught between the teeth with heads crushed, entering like rivers into the ocean and like moths into a blazing fire, while the Lord licks up the worlds with flaming mouths (11.26–30).

Given a divine eye, Arjuna sees the Lord's sovereign form: many mouths and eyes, divine ornaments, garlands and raised weapons, facing every way (11.10–11); the whole world, divided in many ways, standing as one in the body of the god of gods (11.13); the gods, all kinds of beings, Brahmā on the lotus, the seers and divine serpents within it (11.15); no end, middle or beginning (11.16); crowned, with mace and discus, a mass of splendour hard to look at (11.17); sun and moon as eyes, mouth a blazing fire (11.19); the gods entering it and praising it (11.21–22); the warriors of both armies rushing into its tusked mouths and crushed between its teeth (11.26–30).
stage: granted by the Lord's grace through a divine eye (11.8, 11.47)
